title: Trichloroethylene (TCE)
description: High-purity trichloroethylene for metal degreasing and industrial cleaning.

details.longDescription:
Trichloroethylene (TCE, trichloroethene, C2HCl3, CAS 79-01-6) is a non-flammable chlorinated solvent supplied by Global Chemicals LLC at 99.5% minimum purity, stabilised, with a boiling point of 87 °C and specific gravity 1.46, in 200 L drums and 1,000 L IBCs from stock in Muscat, to registered industrial accounts with the occupational-health controls described below.

TCE is the classic vapour-degreasing solvent. In a vapour degreaser the solvent boils at 87 °C, the parts hang in the vapour zone, the pure solvent condenses on the cold metal and runs off carrying mineral oil, cutting fluid, drawing lubricant and machining residue with it, and the parts leave dry and clean enough for plating, bonding, painting or inspection. Its high density and low surface tension reach blind holes and tube bundles, which is why precision engineering, aerospace maintenance, electronics and heat-exchanger shops in Oman specify it; it also serves for cold cleaning of heavy grease and tar. The stabiliser package matters: it neutralises the acid that forms when hot TCE meets aluminium, light and moisture, so the solvent stays usable and the machine stays free of corrosion. Test acid acceptance regularly and never let water into the sump.

Health and regulation: TCE is classified by IARC as carcinogenic to humans (Group 1) and carries strict occupational exposure limits. Modern practice confines it to closed or enclosed degreasing machines with refrigerated freeboards and solvent recovery, local exhaust ventilation, and monitoring of operator exposure; open tanks and brush cleaning are not acceptable uses. Users in Oman must comply with the Environment Authority's requirements for storage, emissions and waste solvent, which goes to a licensed recycler, never to drain. We supply the safety data sheet, a COSHH-style assessment and handling guidance with every order, and we will discuss perchloroethylene or modified-alcohol alternatives where the process allows.

Storage: keep drums sealed, cool, dry and out of sunlight, away from strong alkalis and reactive metals; use steel or stainless equipment, never aluminium for storage, and wear laminate or PVA gloves, goggles and respiratory protection for open handling. Every lot carries a certificate of analysis giving purity, stabiliser content, acidity and water.

Delivery is same day within Muscat, next day to Sohar, two to three days to Salalah and Duqm, and by road across the GCC. Request a quote with the quantity, pack type and the degreasing equipment it will feed.

faqs.question: What is trichloroethylene used for in Oman's industrial sector?
faqs.answer: Trichloroethylene (TCE, trichloroethene, CAS 79-01-6) is a chlorinated solvent primarily used as a metal degreasing agent in Oman's engineering, aerospace, and manufacturing sector. Its high solvency for oils, greases, and waxes, combined with its low boiling point (87°C) and non-flammability, made it the standard vapour degreasing solvent for precision metal parts cleaning in defence, aerospace, and electronic manufacturing. In vapour degreasing equipment (open-top and closed-top degreasing tanks), TCE is heated to boiling, and the rising solvent vapour condenses on cool metal parts, dissolving contamination and draining back as clean solvent. However, TCE is now subject to significant regulatory restriction: the European Union has phased it out under REACH (Annex XIV authorisation required), and the US EPA classifies it as carcinogenic to humans by all routes of exposure and has moved to ban most uses under TSCA. In Oman, TCE use should comply with GHS hazard communication, exposure limits (EU binding OEL 10 ppm 8-hour TWA, 30 ppm STEL), and biological monitoring protocols. Alternatives, depending on the process, include modified alcohols, hydrofluoroether or HFO-based solvents and, under its own controls, perchloroethylene. Global Chemicals LLC supplies TCE with full regulatory documentation.

title: Perchloroethylene (PCE)
description: Industrial perchloroethylene for dry cleaning and metal degreasing.

details.longDescription:
Perchloroethylene (tetrachloroethylene, PCE, perc, C2Cl4, CAS 127-18-4) is a clear, colourless, non-flammable chlorinated solvent supplied by Global Chemicals LLC at 99.9% minimum purity, stabilised against attack on aluminium and iron, with a boiling point of 121 °C and specific gravity 1.62, in 200 L drums and 1,000 L IBCs from stock in Muscat and Rusayl Industrial Area, to dry-cleaning and industrial accounts with the controls described below.

Dry cleaning. Perc is the standard dry-cleaning solvent because it dissolves oils, grease and most stains without water, so fabrics do not shrink, felt or lose colour, and it is non-flammable, which older petroleum solvents are not. Modern closed-circuit machines wash, extract, dry and recover the solvent by condensation and distillation, so a well-run plant loses little perc per load and the still residue is the only waste. Spot removal and pre-spotting use it neat. In metal finishing, perc is the vapour-degreasing solvent for heavy waxes, buffing compounds and oils that trichloroethylene's lower boiling point will not shift, and for cold cleaning of automotive and engineering parts; it is also an intermediate for fluorocarbon refrigerants.

Health and regulation: perchloroethylene is classified by IARC as probably carcinogenic (Group 2A) and carries occupational exposure limits. It belongs in closed machines and enclosed degreasers with solvent recovery and local exhaust ventilation, never in open tanks or for hand wiping; operators should be monitored, and spent solvent, still residue and filters go to a licensed waste contractor in line with the Environment Authority's requirements. We supply the safety data sheet, a COSHH-style assessment and handling guidance with every order, and we can discuss hydrocarbon or modified-alcohol alternatives for new installations.

Storage and handling: keep drums sealed, cool and shaded, away from strong alkalis, reactive metals and open flames or hot surfaces, which decompose it to acid gases; use steel or stainless equipment and PVA or laminate gloves, goggles and respiratory protection for open handling; test acid acceptance in machines regularly so the stabiliser package is not exhausted. Every lot carries a certificate of analysis giving purity, acidity, water and stabiliser content.

Delivery is same day within Muscat, next day to Sohar, two to three days to Salalah and Duqm, and by road across the GCC with a certificate of origin. Request a quote with the quantity, pack type and the machine it will feed.

faqs.question: What is perchloroethylene and what are its applications in Oman?
faqs.answer: Perchloroethylene (PCE, tetrachloroethylene, PERC, CAS 127-18-4) is a chlorinated solvent with excellent stability, non-flammability, and outstanding degreasing power. In Oman, PCE has two primary applications: dry cleaning solvent — PCE is the dominant solvent in commercial dry-cleaning machines (Oman's dry cleaners, hotel laundries, and garment care operations), where it cleans fabrics without water, removing oils, greases, and stains that water-based cleaning cannot address; and metal degreasing and vapour degreasing for precision parts in engineering and electronics manufacturing. PCE has a boiling point of 121°C, is denser than water (1.62 g/mL), and does not absorb water from the air, making it ideal for closed-circuit degreasing systems. PCE is classified as a probable human carcinogen (IARC Group 2A) and is subject to stringent exposure limits (e.g. ACGIH TLV 25 ppm TWA, 100 ppm STEL; EU limit 20 ppm TWA) and emission controls. Oman dry cleaning operations should use closed-loop machines to prevent PCE evaporative emissions and must comply with waste solvent disposal requirements. Global Chemicals LLC supplies perchloroethylene with SDS and regulatory compliance documentation.

title: Methylene Chloride (Industrial Grade)
description: Industrial methylene chloride for paint stripping and industrial cleaning.

details.longDescription:
Methylene chloride (dichloromethane, DCM, CH2Cl2, CAS 75-09-2) is a clear, colourless chlorinated solvent supplied by Global Chemicals LLC at 99% minimum purity in industrial grade, with a boiling point of 40 °C, specific gravity 1.33 and no flash point by standard test, in 200 L drums and 1,000 L IBCs from stock in Muscat, to registered industrial accounts; a higher-purity grade for laboratory and extraction use is listed separately.

It is a fast, powerful paint and coating stripper. DCM penetrates and swells polyurethane, epoxy, powder and multi-layer coatings so they lift from metal, wood and concrete in minutes without attacking the substrate, which is why maintenance painters, shipyards and aircraft maintenance shops across Oman use DCM-based strippers, usually thickened to a gel with a wax or evaporation retarder so the solvent stays on vertical surfaces long enough to work. It removes adhesives, graffiti and cured sealants, degreases and prepares metal before coating, is the solvent in contact adhesives for PVC and rubber, and serves as a process and cleaning solvent in manufacturing. The neat solvent evaporates very fast and leaves no residue, but wax-thickened strippers leave a film that must be washed off before recoating.

Health and regulation: DCM is classified by IARC as probably carcinogenic (Group 2A), it is metabolised to carbon monoxide in the body, and its heavy vapour collects in pits, tanks and enclosed rooms, where it has caused fatalities during stripping work. Many jurisdictions restrict DCM strippers to trained professional and industrial users, and that is how we supply it: with the safety data sheet, a COSHH-style assessment and exposure guidance, for use with forced ventilation or in enclosed equipment, never in confined spaces without air monitoring and supplied-air protection. Although it has no flash point, its vapour can burn in air at high concentration, so keep it away from open flames and hot surfaces, which also decompose it to acid gases.

Storage and handling: keep drums sealed, cool and shaded, because the 40 °C boiling point means pressure builds in a hot container; use steel equipment, never aluminium or light-alloy containers, pumps or spray parts, which DCM can attack, and PVA or laminate gloves, which DCM does not penetrate as it does nitrile; collect spent stripper and sludge as hazardous waste for a licensed contractor. Every lot ships with a certificate of analysis giving purity, acidity, water and stabiliser content.

Delivery is same day within Muscat, next day to Sohar, two to three days to Salalah and Duqm, and by road across the GCC with a certificate of origin. Request a quote with the quantity, pack type and intended use.
